natural_language_statement:
For a natural number $k$, consider subsets $S$ of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ containing no distinct $a<b<c$ with $1/a=1/b+1/c$. The attainable cardinality thresholds at 731 and 732 coincide:

$$
\exists S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,732\},\ S\text{ admissible},\ |S|\geq k\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,731\},\ S\text{ admissible},\ |S|\geq k.
$$

This is a finite plateau result and does not assume a numerical value of the extremal function at 731. It does not settle the asymptotic Erdős problem 302; no first-discovery claim is made.

 (∃ S : Nat → Bool, RatAdmissible 732 S ∧ k ≤ cardinal S) ↔
 (∃ S : Nat → Bool, RatAdmissible 731 S ∧ k ≤ cardinal S) := by sorry
